prompt.spicy:
One behaviour, thirty days. Not a goal — a Cue and a Behaviour, because "try harder" has a measured effect of roughly nothing and if–then plans don't.

Pick one of ours or write your own. Small enough that you'd do it on a bad day.
prompt.boardroom:
One behaviour, thirty days. Not a goal but a Cue and a Behaviour: general intention has minimal measured effect, whereas if–then planning does not.

Select one of the suggestions or write your own. It should be small enough to complete on a difficult day.

cue.spicy: When I notice I've been stuck for 15 minutes
cue.boardroom: When I have been stuck for 15 minutes

behaviour.spicy: I write the one-sentence version of where I'm stuck before I ask anyone
behaviour.boardroom: I write a one-sentence statement of the blocker before escalating

cue.spicy: When a task feels vague and I want to close the tab
cue.boardroom: When a task feels unclear and I am inclined to defer it

behaviour.spicy: I do the smallest visible piece of it for ten minutes
behaviour.boardroom: I complete the smallest concrete part of it for ten minutes

cue.spicy: When I'm about to send "any update on this?"
cue.boardroom: When I am about to send a reminder containing no decision

behaviour.spicy: I add what I'll do by default if nobody replies
behaviour.boardroom: I add the action I will take by default if there is no response

cue.spicy: When someone says "no rush" about something I haven't started
cue.boardroom: When someone indicates there is no urgency on work I have not started

behaviour.spicy: I say the specific thing I'm stuck on, right then, in that conversation
behaviour.boardroom: I state the specific blocker in that conversation

verdict.spicy: In the tracker. Four check-ins over thirty days, then it ends. It genuinely ends — this isn't a streak and nothing breaks if you miss a Tuesday.
verdict.boardroom: Recorded in the tracker with four check-ins across thirty days, after which it concludes. Missed days do not reset anything.

principle.spicy: Cue → Behaviour. The cue is the part people leave out, and it's the part that works.
principle.boardroom: Cue then Behaviour. The cue is the component most often omitted and the one that produces the effect.
